signatures.name: above_chance_discovery
signatures.description: Successful combinations occur at a rate above the empirical random-agent baseline of ~0.30 (Monte Carlo sim of random pair selection from inventory; the four base elements participate in many recipes so even random play succeeds often). Brändle et al. report 0.40-0.50 success rates for adult humans.

signatures.name: empowerment_preference
signatures.description: On each attempt, the average in-degree of the chosen pair (how many recipes use these elements) positively correlates with whether the attempt succeeds. Brändle et al.'s headline finding: humans pick high-empowerment elements (Brändle et al. 2023, Nature Human Behaviour, Fig 4).

signatures.name: non_redundant_attempts
signatures.description: Humans avoid retrying the same combination — most attempts use a pair not yet attempted. Quantified via the proportion of attempts whose pair (a_idx, b_idx) is unique up to that trial. A truly random combiner would repeat pairs (and thus is_unique_pair=true) close to 1.0 only at the very start; over a long session a strategic agent maintains a high unique-pair rate.
